notes.note: Reading 2 chosen: any data type (basic, structured, subtype, array, anytype) may be a message type; non-data types are not used. A subtype of a type already listed was avoided because tools treat it as a duplicate message type.
Needs a SUT, so noexecution: only checks that call/getreply over a port mapped to the system interface is accepted.
Needs a SUT, so noexecution: checks that the test system can both call a procedure in the SUT (out signature) and accept a call from the SUT (in signature, getcall/reply) on a mapped port.
Reading 1 chosen (signature defined in some module); the test references a signature that is defined nowhere.
Syntax reading chosen: type and identifier are mandatory, the direction is optional; the test mixes parameters with and without direction.
Reading 1 chosen (exceptions): a range template is used in a catch operation to check the raised exception.
Tested as a negative test: since the list defines all possible exception types, raising a type not in the list is rejected.
Non-blocking use of a signature without noblock is shown by a call without response handling part and without nowait (cf. 22.3.1 restriction j).

Titan accepts a component type as signature return type; per the definitions in clause 3 component types are not data types (they are listed separately in 'component data types'), so the reject verdict is kept.
Reading 2 chosen: templates for component data types (incl. a component type) and a signature. anytype omitted since Titan needs an extension attribute for anytype fields.
Titan does not support the @deterministic modifier on templates (syntax error); test is correct per 15.3 syntax.
Titan does not support @deterministic templates. The template is evaluated twice in the same snapshot (alt guard and receive); equality of results is only observable indirectly via a pass verdict.
Uses the standard's own example (union containing a record with a default field). Titan does not implement this restriction.
Local template initialized from an uninitialized template variable; Titan does not detect this statically. A tool might only detect it at runtime.
Titan does not implement the restriction on out/inout function calls in fuzzy template bodies.
Reading 1 chosen: a fuzzy template passed to a @fuzzy formal template parameter keeps its fuzzy feature (re-evaluated at each reference).
Titan rejects only because it lacks @deterministic template syntax, not because of the rnd() call; the test violates restriction g) via 16.1.4 f).
